provenance.label: Synthetic example
provenance.description: Quotes refer to the bundled original toy article. Quote matching verifies traceability; it is not independent scientific review.

source.locator_convention: One-based physical lines, matching scripts/project.py text import.

claims.text: Different group weights can reverse the pooled ordering in this synthetic example.

evidence.quote: This synthetic example illustrates how pooling groups with different weights can reverse an observed comparison.

claims.text: The easy-group observed rates are A 90% and B 95%.

evidence.quote: In the easy group, the success rates are 90% for A and 95% for B.
In the easy group, option A has 90 successes in 100 trials and option B has 19 successes in 20 trials.

claims.text: The hard-group observed rates are A 10% and B 20%.

evidence.quote: In the hard group, they are 10% for A and 20% for B.
In the hard group, option A has 1 success in 10 trials and option B has 20 successes in 100 trials.

claims.text: Pooling gives A approximately 82.7% and B 32.5%, reversing the group-level ordering because their group mixtures differ.

evidence.quote: After pooling, A has 91 successes in 110 trials, approximately 82.7%, while B has 39 successes in 120 trials, or 32.5%.
The pooled ordering reverses because A has a larger proportion of easy-group trials and B has a larger proportion of hard-group trials.

claims.text: A common 50:50 group mixture gives A 50% and B 57.5%; this is a different summary from the observed pooled rates.

evidence.quote: With a common 50:50 weighting of easy and hard groups, the standardized rates are 50% for A and 57.5% for B.
These standardized rates describe a common group mixture, not the observed pooled mixtures.

claims.text: Compare the groups and their weights before judging the overall rate.

evidence.quote: Compare the groups and their weights before judging the overall rate.

scenes.display_text: The overall rate can hide a reversal.
scenes.spoken_text: Synthetic example: the overall rate can hide a reversal.
scenes.visual_intent: Introduce A and B and clearly label the entire demonstration Synthetic example.

scenes.spoken_text: In the easy group, B scores ninety-five percent, versus ninety percent for A.
scenes.visual_intent: Reveal easy-group denominators and corresponding rates, with B above A.

scenes.spoken_text: In the hard group, B also leads: twenty percent, versus ten percent for A.
scenes.visual_intent: Switch to hard-group counts and rates, preserving option colors and the comparison scale.

scenes.spoken_text: Pool the counts, and A appears ahead. A has far more easy trials; B has far more hard trials.
scenes.visual_intent: Show the observed group weights before revealing pooled rates; never imply a causal advantage.

scenes.spoken_text: Give both groups equal weight. The rates become fifty percent for A and fifty-seven point five percent for B.
scenes.visual_intent: Replace unequal observed group mixtures with explicit equal weights; distinguish this standardized summary from observed pooling.

scenes.display_text: Compare the groups and their weights before judging the overall rate.
scenes.spoken_text: Compare the groups and their weights before judging the overall rate.
scenes.visual_intent: Finish with one short takeaway and the persistent Synthetic example label.
